extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent owners/agents participating in ex parte reexamination proceedings (including third-party requesters and their representatives)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for examiners and parties on handling service, defective papers, entry/expungement of submissions, petitions to revive, and preparation/issuance of final actions in ex parte reexamination proceedings under the MPEP and relevant CFR/USC provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling late amendments when time for response has expired
rubrics_metrics.description: When time has expired for response, entry of an amendment is within the discretion of the examiner. However, the examiner should recognize that substantial patent rights will be at issue with no opportunity for the patent owner to refile under 37 CFR 1.53(b) or 1.53(d) nor to file a request for continued examination under 37 CFR 1.114. Thus, where the time has expired for response and the amendment submitted would place the proceeding in condition for issuance of a reexamination certificate except for an omission through apparent oversight or inadvertence, the examiner should follow this course of action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider exercising discretion to enter/correct where omission was oversight/inadvertence because reexamination is finalizing substantial rights; be mindful that patent owner lacks usual continuation/RCX options in reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defects constituting an informal (defective) submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Even if the substance of a submission is complete, the submission can be defective (an 'informal submission'). Defects include: (A) paper does not include proof of service; (B) paper is unsigned; (C) paper is signed by a non-practitioner who is not of record; (D) amendment filed by patent owner does not comply with 37 CFR 1.530(d)-(j); (E) amendment does not comply with 37 CFR 1.20(c)(3) and/or 37 CFR 1.20(c)(4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other defects not listed may be designated via the 'other' box on notification forms; give examples (e.g., response on easily erasable paper) and explain specifics where needed on an attached sheet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forms and procedure for notifying defective papers (PTOL-475 / PTO-2311)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a submission made prior to final rejection is defective (informal), forms PTOL-475 and PTO-2311 are used to provide notification of the defects present in the submission. PTOL-475 notifies defects in submissions in a third-party requested reexamination; PTO-2311 notifies defects in a patent owner requested ex parte reexamination (including 35 U.S.C. 257) or Director-ordered ex parte reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Often only check the appropriate box and fill blanks; if the defect needs further clarification (e.g., specifics of noncompliance with 37 CFR 1.530(d)-(j)), set forth additional information on a separate sheet attached to the form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time to correct defects and extensions; consequences if not corrected
rubrics_metrics.description: A time period from the mailing date of the notice will be set in the appropriate form (PTOL-475 or PTO-2311) for correction of the defect(s). Extension of time to correct the defect(s) may be requested under 37 CFR 1.550(c). If the defect is not corrected, the submission will not be entered. If failure to comply with the notice results in a patent owner failure to file a timely and appropriate response to any Office action, prosecution of the reexamination proceeding generally will be terminated under 37 CFR 1.550(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a defective response is filed after final rejection (but before expiration), issue advisory Office action (PTOL-467 / PTOL-467A) rather than PTOL-475/PT O-2311; time periods in final rejection continue to run and may be extended per MPEP § 2265.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling defective responses filed after final rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: If a defective (informal) response to an examiner’s action is filed after final rejection (before expiration of the permissible response period), the examiner should not issue PTOL-475 or PTO-2311. Rather, an advisory Office action (PTOL-467 or PTOL-467A) should be issued with an explanation of the defect (informality). The time period set in the final rejection continues to run and is extended by two months if the response is the first response after the final rejection in accordance with MPEP § 2265.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use advisory action forms and follow final rejection timing rules; see MPEP § 2272 for related guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate/proof of service requirement for third-party requested reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Any request for reexamination must include a certification that a copy of the request filed by a person other than the patent owner has been served in its entirety on the patent owner at the address provided in § 1.33(c). The name and address of the party served must be indicated. If service was not possible, a duplicate copy must be supplied to the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After filing of a request for ex parte reexamination by a third party requester, any document filed by either party must be served on the other in the manner provided by § 1.248; the document must reflect service or it may be refused consideration by the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof of service content and required handling when missing
rubrics_metrics.description: As proof of service, the party submitting the paper to the Office must attach a certificate of service to the paper. It is required that the name and address of the party served, and the method of service be set forth in the certificate of service. A copy of the certificate must be attached with the copy of the paper served on the other party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Papers filed without required proof of service may be denied consideration. The Central Reexamination Unit (CRU) should contact the submitting party by telephone to confirm whether service was inadvertently omitted; if service is confirmed, the submission is entered and annotated 'Service confirmed by [name] on [date]'. If no service was made or the submitter cannot be contacted, the submission is normally not considered and annotated in the IFW as 'N/E' with 'no service'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice paragraph for lack of service (form paragraph 22.15)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a submission was not served as required in a third-party requester reexamination proceeding, notify the submitting party that the submission is defective for lack of service and require service and a certificate within a shortened statutory period of ONE MONTH or THIRTY DAYS, whichever is longer, from the mailing date of the letter. If service is not timely made, the submission may be denied consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use cover sheet PTOL-473 and do not use PTOL-475 for responses to a final rejection lacking proof of service; instead use advisory Office action forms as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of failure to serve submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure of a party to serve a submission in response to a notice may have the following consequences: (A) For a patent owner statement or third party reply, the submission may be refused consideration and will not be addressed in the reexamination proceeding other than to inform parties of lack of consideration; (B) For a patent owner response to an Office action, the response may be refused consideration and the prosecution of the proceeding will be terminated in accordance with 37 CFR 1.550(d), unless the patent owner has otherwise completely responded to the Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See relevant MPEP sections for handling initial third-party requests, owner statements, and third-party replies (MPEP §§ 2220, 2249, 2251, 2266).

rubrics_metrics.name: Expungement and disposition of inappropriate (unauthorized/improper) papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers filed during reexamination proceedings that are inappropriate because of some defect will be expunged from the official file by marking them 'closed' and 'non-public'. If an inappropriate paper has already been scanned into the IFW, it cannot be physically returned but will be expunged (marked non-public/closed) so it does not appear in the active IFW public record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expungement reduces unnecessary material in the public record and complies with regulations that certain papers will not be considered or acknowledged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categories of papers to be expunged (owner, requester, third party)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific types of papers are to be expunged/destroyed: For owner filings (e.g., premature response by owner filed prior to an order to reexamine will not be considered and will be expunged; papers submitted on behalf of a third party as owner filings will be expunged). For requester filings (§ 1.535): requester replies when no owner statement filed (inappropriate), late requester responses more than 2 months after service of owner's statement, and any additional requester participation beyond the reply will be expunged. For third parties (§ 1.501, § 1.565(a)): unless the paper raises only issues appropriate under 37 CFR 1.501 or consists solely of a prior decision on the patent by another forum, it will be destroyed or expunged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit iterative filings/oppositions to preserve special dispatch of reexamination; petitions to deny extensions by requester will be expunged since requester lacks participation rights to that extent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of defective papers to be retained in the reexamination file
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain defective papers are retained in the reexamination file (not expunged) and annotated: Owner—unsigned papers, papers signed by fewer than all owners, papers lacking proof of service where proof is required (may be denied consideration), untimely papers filed after response period. Requester—unsigned papers; papers without proof of service where proof is required may be denied consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retained papers should be appropriately annotated in the IFW to reflect the defect and whether considered or not.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revival of terminated reexamination prosecution for unintentional delay (petition under 37 CFR 1.137 / 35 U.S.C. 27)
rubrics_metrics.description: An ex parte reexamination prosecution terminated under 37 CFR 1.550(d) can be revived if the delay in response by the patent owner (or failure to timely file an interview statement) was unintentional in accordance with 37 CFR 1.137 and 35 U.S.C. 27.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A grantable petition under 37 CFR 1.137 must be accompanied by: (1) the reply required to the outstanding Office action or notice (unless previously filed); (2) the petition fee per § 1.17(m); (3) any terminal disclaimer (and fee) required; and (4) a statement that the entire delay from due date until filing of petition was unintentional. The Director may require additional information if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition based on unavoidable delay is no longer available
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.137 was revised (PLTIA implementation) to eliminate petitions based on 'unavoidable' delay and to provide for revival only on the basis of unintentional delay. This change applies to applications and reexamination proceedings regardless of filing dates (effective Dec 18, 2013).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely on 'unavoidable delay' petitions; use unintentional delay petition procedures and fees under 37 CFR 1.137 and 35 U.S.C. 27.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconsideration requirements (responding to Office action)
rubrics_metrics.description: To be entitled to reconsideration, the patent owner must respond to the Office action (37 CFR 1.111(b)). The patent owner may respond with or without amendment and the patent under reexamination will be reconsidered, and so on repeatedly unless the examiner has indicated the action is final (see 37 CFR 1.112). Any amendment after the second Office action, which will normally be final as provided in MPEP § 2271, must ordinarily be restricted to the rejection or to the objection or requirement made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow timing and amendment limitations for responses after final actions; provide complete responses to facilitate reconsideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clerical handling and entry of amendments; treatment of new matter and claim scope changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments submitted with a request under 35 U.S.C. 302, or after reexamination is ordered under 35 U.S.C. 304 or 257, which comply with 37 CFR 1.530(d)-(j), will generally be entered in the reexamination file if submitted prior to a final action. Any 'new matter' amendment to the disclosure (35 U.S.C. 132) will be required to be canceled, and claims containing new matter will be rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112. A 'new matter' amendment to the drawing is ordinarily not entered. Where an amendment enlarges the scope of the claims of the patent, the amendment will be entered; however the appropriate claims will be rejected under 35 U.S.C. 305.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §§ 2234, 2250, 608.04(a,c) for detailed entry procedures; entry for purposes of reexamination does not give legal effect until certificate issuance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria and procedures for making a final Office action in reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Before a final action, a clear issue should be developed between the examiner and the patent owner. The examiner will twice provide the patent owner with information and references useful in defining the Office's position as to unpatentability. The first Office action should identify substantial new questions of patentability and fully apply relevant grounds of rejection. The second Office action will generally be made final; criteria for finality are analogous to MPEP § 706.07(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final rejection must carefully review all outstanding grounds, reiterate any relied grounds, and be developed sufficiently for the patent owner to judge appealability. If a prior Office action contains a complete statement of a ground, the final may refer to it but should rebut patent owner arguments. Prepare panel review conference per MPEP § 2271.01; final action must be signed by primary examiner and conferees initial; conclude with form paragraphs 22.09 or 22.10 and observe shortened statutory periods and extension rules per 37 CFR 1.550(c) and MPEP § 2265.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of art cited by patent owner during prosecution
rubrics_metrics.description: Where art is submitted in a prior art citation under 37 CFR 1.501 and/or 37 CFR 1.555 (IDS in reexamination is construed as a prior art citation) and the submission is not accompanied by a statement similar to 37 CFR 1.97(e), the examiner may use the submitted art and make the next Office action final whether or not the claims have been amended, provided no other new ground of rejection is introduced based on new art not cited in the prior art citation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If patent owner submits art without required statements, examiner may finalize based on that art; ensure no other new grounds are introduced that would improperly surprise the owner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signatory authority for final Office actions
rubrics_metrics.description: As with all other Office correspondence on the merits in a reexamination proceeding, the final Office action must be signed by a primary examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure appropriate signature and conferee initials where panel review was used; follow procedural formalities for final actions.
